pattern.top_pattern: California spend is concentrated in a small number of very high-cost inpatient and post-acute cases
pattern.what_is_impacting: CA / EPO / ACUTE HOSPITAL, LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL, Physical Rehab / IP Med/Surg and NF
key_driver_codes: Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC
Degenerative Nervous System Disorders without MCC
ENC ORTHOPED AFTERCARE FLW SURG AMP
pattern.pattern_details: California cost growth is concentrated in a small set of high-cost inpatient neuroscience and orthopedic aftercare cases, and the same cases extend into EPO post-acute settings. Acute hospital EPO craniotomy pressure is paired with added spend in long term care hospital and physical rehab settings. This looks like concentrated high-severity case mix carrying across the care continuum, not broad-based utilization inflation.
pattern.why_it_matters: These cases can create outsized spend through both the index admission and downstream post-acute placements.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Launch a combined clinical, UM, and reimbursement review of CA high-cost inpatient cases and their post-acute transitions, with special focus on neurosurgery and orthopedic aftercare pathways.
pattern.validation_reason: Most contributing cases are low-volume, high-cost outliers, so case-level validation is needed before broader policy action.
evidence_summary: CA high-cost inpatient and post-acute patterns contributed about $8.6M.
Rare CA IP Med/Surg cases added about $5.5M.
CA EPO acute hospital craniotomy cases added about $2.1M.
CA EPO long term care hospital and physical rehab cases added about $0.9M combined.
